Renegade
REN-ih-gayd
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
From Spanish renegado and Medieval Latin renegatus, one who has denied (renegare) — originally a Christian who renounced the faith, especially to convert to Islam; then any deserter or rebel. In late 2019 the word became a dance: Jalaiah Harmon, a fourteen-year-old in Atlanta, choreographed "the Renegade" to the rapper K Camp’s song "Lottery," and it spread through TikTok, made famous by bigger creators who did not credit her until a February 2020 newspaper story did. Parents should know the song’s lyrics are explicit.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To Gen Alpha, the Renegade is the fast arm-and-hand TikTok dance from 2020. Many children learned it from older siblings or school friends. The Christian observation: two lessons hide in this one word. The first is about credit. A fourteen-year-old girl made the dance, and famous creators got the fame until a newspaper set the record straight. Scripture commands the opposite: "Render therefore to all their dues... honour to whom honour" (Rom 13:7). The second lesson is the word itself. A renegade was first a Christian who denied Christ — the very thing Peter did by the fire, three times, and then "went out, and wept bitterly" (Luk 22:62). The Bible warns, "Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God" (Heb 3:12), and records the sad line "Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world" (2Ti 4:10). But Peter’s story shows the gospel’s mercy: the denier was restored and fed the flock. A father can tell a five-year-old: "Renegade means someone who leaves God’s team. Peter did that once, and he was so sorry, and Jesus forgave him. Let’s always stay close to Jesus." And he should know the song before the dance comes home.

Webster 1828 Definition

Old word for one who denies the faith, turned TikTok dance (Jalaiah Harmon, 2019–20) — a lesson in giving honor where it is due and in the apostasy the word first named.

RENEGADE, n. (Spanish renegado; English 16th c.; TikTok dance, 2019–present) Originally, one who denies the faith; a deserter or rebel; now also the viral dance. "Can you do the Renegade?"

The dance: choreographed by Jalaiah Harmon (Atlanta, 2019) to K Camp’s "Lottery" (explicit lyrics).

Adj. use: rebellious, lawless ("a renegade cop").

Decode for parents: the dance is fine; the song is not; the word’s first meaning is apostasy.

Key Scripture

Rom 13:7 — "Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour."

Luk 22:62 — "And Peter went out, and wept bitterly."

Heb 3:12 — "Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God."

2Ti 4:10 — "For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia."

Modern Corruption

The Renegade dance was taken from the girl who made it and set to an explicit song; the word itself first named the man who denies Christ — a warning answered by Peter’s restoration.

expand to see more

The dance’s story is a parable of the attention economy: the inventor anonymous, the imitators famous. Children who learn the dance rarely know whose it was. And the song it rides on, like much of the music behind viral dances, carries lyrics no parent would choose. A child can learn a dance from a sibling and a vocabulary from the soundtrack.

The deeper lesson is in the dictionary. A renegade denied the faith. Scripture’s warnings against falling away are real, and so is its mercy for the fallen: Peter wept, was restored, and was told to feed the sheep. Teach your child to give credit, to choose clean songs, and to stay on the Lord’s side — and that if he ever runs, the way home is open.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Medieval Latin renegare (to deny) → Spanish renegado (apostate) → English renegade → the Renegade dance (TikTok, 2019–20).

expand to see more

Latin re- + negare — to deny again, renounce

Spanish renegado — a Christian who renounced the faith

English renegade (16th c.) — apostate, deserter, rebel

Late 2019: Jalaiah Harmon’s dance to K Camp’s "Lottery"

February 2020: a newspaper story credits Harmon; NBA All-Star performance follows

Usage

""I learned the Renegade from my cousin, but Mom said not that song.""

"Render honour to whom honour — the girl who made the dance (Rom 13:7)."

"Peter denied and wept bitterly, and was restored; that is the gospel for every renegade (Luk 22:62)."
